Routine Coverage by Dose and Year

Source: R/vaccination_inputs.R
routine_dose_coverage.Rd

Turns the processed routine coverage data into one coverage series per modelled dose, covering every model year.

Usage

routine_dose_coverage(vaccination_data, n_doses, years, percent = TRUE)

Arguments

vaccination_data

Processed routine vaccination data with columns `year`, `dose_order` and `coverage`.

n_doses

Number of doses the model represents.

years

Model years.

percent

Logical; is `coverage` in percent (WHO data) rather than a proportion (custom data)?

Value

A matrix of coverage proportions with one row per year and one column per dose. The attribute `interpolated_doses` lists doses whose coverage was taken from neighbouring doses and `last_data_year` gives the last year with data for each dose.

Details

* Coverage is zero before the first year with data, interpolated linearly across gaps, and carried forward after the last year with data. * A dose with no data that sits between two doses with data is given the mean of its neighbours. WUENIC reports DTP1 and DTP3 only, so this is how the second DTP dose gets a coverage (in 0.1.0 it had none, and nobody in the model could progress beyond one dose). * Doses beyond the number the model represents (for example the fourth, fifth and sixth diphtheria doses) are dropped: the model has no strata for them. * Coverage of a dose is not allowed to exceed coverage of the dose before it.
